name: Marketmore Cucumber
summary: The catalog records Marketmore type within Cucumis sativus. The cultivation guidance is cucumber-level; cultivar-specific dimensions, performance and indoor-system advice are not established here.

identity.short: Marketmore type is recorded within Cucumis sativus
identity.guidance: The catalog records Marketmore type under Cucumis sativus. The home-garden sources used in this profile provide cucumber-level guidance; they do not establish cultivar-specific dimensions, disease resistance or hydroponic settings.

pruning.short: Guide vines gently; avoid routine pruning assumptions
pruning.guidance: UMN Extension notes that some cucumber varieties form long vines and may use a trellis. Guide a vining plant onto support without damaging stems; this crop guidance does not establish a Marketmore-specific pruning regimen or prove indoor-system suitability.

cultivation.short: Keep the root zone evenly moist in warm growing conditions
cultivation.guidance: Cucumbers are warm-weather crops. UMN Extension recommends moisture-retentive yet well-drained soil and thorough watering while keeping foliage dry; its Minnesota soil and weekly water guidance is regional outdoor context, not a hydroponic recipe.

care.short: Protect shallow vine roots during maintenance
care.guidance: Cucumber roots include surface branches, and vines may root at their joints. Weed shallowly and avoid repeatedly shifting or lifting established vines; this reduces avoidable root and stem disturbance rather than prescribing a pruning schedule.

harvest.short: Pick at the intended slicer size before fruits overmature
harvest.guidance: UMN Extension advises harvesting cucumber slicers before fruits become overlarge, yellow-skinned, and full of large seeds. Pick often and handle the vine gently; leaving oversized fruit can reduce continued yield. This is species/crop guidance, not a Marketmore-specific size threshold.

problems.short: Check pollination and moisture before diagnosing poor fruit
problems.guidance: Poor fruit set can follow inadequate pollination, including during cold, rainy, or cloudy weather. UMN Extension also notes that cucumber bitterness varies among varieties and can be more noticeable near the blossom end. In humid conditions, angular yellow leaf spots with gray-purple growth underneath can be a downy-mildew warning; symptoms can resemble other disorders, so do not treat this as a diagnosis or cultivar-resistance claim.

flowering.short: Early male flowers normally precede fruit-bearing female flowers
flowering.guidance: Cucumber plants produce separate male and female flowers on the same plant. Male flowers commonly appear first; female flowers have a small ovary behind the bloom and need pollen transfer for fruit development. Early flower drop alone is therefore not proof of a plant problem.

pruning.guidance: UMN Extension describes bush cucumber types as having very short vines and fitting smaller gardens better than long-vining forms. That type-level distinction does not establish an exact footprint or eliminate the need to inspect the actual plant as fruit develops.

cultivation.guidance: Cucumbers grow best in warm weather. UMN Extension recommends soil that holds moisture but drains well and thorough watering that avoids wetting foliage; Minnesota calendars and field watering amounts are not universal instructions for other climates or indoor systems.

care.short: Maintain moisture and avoid injuring surface roots
care.guidance: Check the root zone regularly during active growth. Cucumber roots branch near the soil surface, so shallow hand-weeding is safer than deep cultivation close to the plant. This is outdoor crop care, not hydroponic guidance.

harvest.short: Frequent picking supports a continuing harvest
harvest.guidance: Harvest fruits at the size appropriate to their intended use and before they become overlarge and yellow. Pick regularly and handle the plant gently; leaving oversized cucumbers on the vine can lower yield. No fixed mature spread or harvest date is assigned to this bush type.

problems.short: Poor fruit set can be a pollination issue
problems.guidance: Cucumber flowers need pollen transfer for fruit set; cold, rainy, or cloudy conditions may reduce pollination. Bitterness can vary among cucumber varieties. These are general crop risks, not evidence that this bush type has a particular disease or resistance.

flowering.short: Male blooms come first; female blooms carry a tiny ovary
flowering.guidance: In cucumber, male flowers often appear before female flowers. The small swelling behind a female flower is the developing ovary; pollen transfer is needed for fruit development in the typical varieties described by UMN Extension. The first male flowers dropping is normal.

name: Calabrese Broccoli
summary: Calabrese broccoli is a heading-broccoli type of Brassica oleracea. The useful harvest is the tight central cluster of unopened flower buds; cutting it promptly can allow smaller side shoots to follow. Heat and cold history affect head development, and the cited guidance is not cultivar-specific.

identity.short: Calabrese heading broccoli within Brassica oleracea
identity.guidance: This identity is represented as a Calabrese/heading-broccoli type, not a named cultivar. UMN describes standard heading broccoli separately from sprouting types; its generic crop instructions do not establish Calabrese-specific size or heat tolerance.

cultivation.short: A cool-season head crop; keep moisture steady during head development
cultivation.guidance: UMN includes broccoli among cool-season crops and identifies head development as a critical moisture period. Its climate and field guidance are regional outdoor-soil context; this does not establish hydroponic settings or a Calabrese-specific temperature threshold.

growth.short: The central head is a cluster of unopened flower buds
growth.guidance: The edible head is made of small flower buds on a central stalk. Once cut, the plant can form smaller side shoots; the number and timing are not guaranteed for this identity or growing environment.

pruning.short: No routine pruning; remove the central head cleanly at harvest
pruning.guidance: The cited guidance does not prescribe routine pruning. Cut the mature central head with a short stalk and leave the lower plant in place so secondary shoots may develop; this is a harvest cut, not a canopy-shaping regimen.

harvest.short: Cut while buds are tight and green, before they open
harvest.guidance: UMN recommends harvesting broccoli when the head reaches usable size while its buds remain tight and green. Cut the central head with a short stalk; leave the lower plant for side shoots and harvest those when usable. If flowers begin opening, harvest promptly because quality declines.

problems.short: Heat can loosen or open the head; early cold can cause buttoning
problems.guidance: In UMN's regional guidance, high heat after head formation can trigger premature flowering, while cold exposure before enough leafy growth can cause small, misshapen heads (buttoning). Treat these as temperature-related possibilities, not Calabrese-specific susceptibility or a local forecast.
